notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level and no hardware run). Model-authored and unreviewed. The package serves HandLiftEnv-v1 only; HandPushEnv (the other card entry symbol) is not covered. The upstream package was not imported or run: it needs gym, pybullet, numpy, chumpy, transforms3d and the separately downloaded MANO models (README.md:25-29, setup.py:36-43), and its HandLiftEnv constructor passes the environment object as model_path to HandObjectEnv (mano_pybullet/envs/hand_lift_env.py:17). The fake is pure Python and kinematic: it mirrors the default right-hand joint-mode Tuple spaces, the 20 HandModel20 joint angles/velocities/torques, the 6 constraint forces, and the lift reward and done rule; it was not compared with a real PyBullet run. The sim backend (gym.make) was not run. Five warnings are expected of this family and contract: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the seed only affects the next reset and makes no native call), three G8.NO_UNIT for the integer inputs the bridge derives (ticks and seed twice), and G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE because the environment's action space is a gymnasium Tuple, from which the bridge derives structure but no per-element limits, so the suite awards CL2 while every other CL3 test passes. There are no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. No limits are declared and no site-limits overlay is needed: the device is simulated R0, and the action bounds are documented as Facts from mano_pybullet/envs/hand_env.py:73-89. Only catalogue classes are used, so there are no catalogue requests.
